correctness.rationale: A uniform positive probability of no flip and a hit of the open endpoint in a fixed time block gives finite mean absorption. For the two coupled backward equations, mixed homogeneous boundary conditions make the boundary terms vanish on integrating the homogeneous difference equations against the differences of two solutions; the resulting sum of derivative energies and the gate-state difference energy forces both functions to vanish. With t=alpha L/2, the even part of the mean is x(L−x)/(2D)+C and the odd part is B sinh(alpha(x−L/2)). The derivative condition gives B=L/(2D alpha cosh t) and the absorbing value gives C=B sinh t. For the left-exit probability the averaged part is 1/2+c(x−L/2), while the difference part is A cosh(alpha(x−L/2)); the left Neumann and absorbing conditions give c=−A alpha sinh t and A=1/[2(cosh t+t sinh t)], yielding the claimed affine profile. The uniform initial gate is essential to identifying the averaged parts with the observables. In a static model either full-profile match forces equal left and right reactivities: for the mean use equal endpoint values and opposite derivatives, and for the splitting profile use D P'(0)=h_0(P(0)−1), −D P'(L)=h_L P(L), with P(0)−1=−P(L) and P(L)>0. The corresponding constants are D alpha coth t and D alpha tanh t, different at all finite positive rates. Limits and the x-independent penalty follow from these formulas. This is a continuum boundary-value calculation, not a claim of continuum verification by the frozen finite-mesh code.

value.rationale: Time and exit side are natural independent calibration observables for diffusion with absorption. The exact result shows that a standard positive static Robin law with the same diffusivity and geometry cannot reproduce both curves, even allowing unequal endpoints. The strict finite-rate gap is a useful diagnostic of model misspecification despite a common fast-switching limit. It does not claim a guarantee for inference from a single position or cover general intermittency models.
